cards.explanation: The answer is shearing them. Nabal, a wealthy man from Maon, is shearing his sheep in Carmel. The text says he has a thousand goats and three thousand sheep. That's a lot of haircuts, and I can barely keep my own mustache in line.
The answer is False. Abigail is described as an intelligent and beautiful woman. Her husband Nabal, a Calebite, is called harsh and evil in his dealings. Kind and generous isn't on the list, friends.

The answer is a wish for long life and peace. David tells the young men to say, “Long life to you, and peace to you and to your house and to all that belongs to you.” That's a warm hello before any request. I'd take that greeting over a lot of emails I've seen.
The answer is True. David's message says, “Ask your young men, and they will tell you.” He's inviting Nabal to check the story with his own people. He points Nabal to his own workers for the answer.

The answer is whatever he can spare. The message says, “Please give whatever you can spare to your servants and to your son David.” It's a modest ask on a feast day. David doesn't name a number or a price.

The answer is that Nabal asks who David even is. He says, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse?” He answers a friendly greeting with a question that sounds like he's never heard the name. Friends, that's a rough way to answer someone wishing you peace.

The answer is shearers. Nabal says, “Why should I take my bread and water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to these men whose origin I do not know?” He says he doesn't know these men's origin, and that's the question he asks about giving them anything.
The answer is strap on your swords. David says, “Strap on your swords!” And all his men strap them on. Friends, the mood in that camp just changed fast.

The answer is True. Nabal's young man tells Abigail, “They were a wall around us, both day and night, the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.” A wall is a pretty strong picture of being watched over. It's his own worker saying so.

The answer is disaster. The young man says, “…disaster looms over our master and all his household.” He's telling Abigail to think carefully about what she must do. Friends, when a servant says that, you listen.
The answer is False. The text says she “…did not tell her husband Nabal.” She sends her young men ahead and follows right behind them.

The answer is that David has sworn to leave no male of Nabal's alive, and it's a heavy one. He says, “May God punish David, and ever so severely, if I let one male belonging to Nabal survive until morning.” That's a serious oath. I think this is the moment the story holds its breath.
The answer is False. Abigail sees David and quickly gets off the donkey, falls facedown and bows before him. No hiding in the ravine for her.
The answer is True. At David's feet, Abigail says, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you…” She asks to carry the blame herself. Then she asks to be heard.
The answer is Fool. Abigail says of Nabal, “His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him.” That's his own wife speaking, right to David. She says it to ask David to pay him no attention.

The answer is bloodshed. Abigail says the LORD “…has held you back from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand…” She credits the LORD with stopping David. Friends, that's one brave thing to say to a man with four hundred swords.
The answer is a lasting dynasty. Abigail tells David, “…the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles.” She's looking far down the road for him.

The answer is True. Abigail says that when the LORD has done all the good He promised, “…He has appointed you ruler over Israel…” She says it to David face to face. That's a big thing to hear in a ravine.
The answer is that he remember her. Abigail's last request is, “And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your servant.” After all that, it's a small, humble ask.

The answer is the LORD, the God of Israel. David says, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!” He gives the credit to the LORD for the meeting. That's a big turn from a man who was strapping on a sword.

The answer is go home in peace. David says, “Go home in peace. See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.” He receives what she brought and sends her off in peace. That's his answer after hearing her out.

The answer is True. Abigail finds Nabal in high spirits and very drunk, so she tells him nothing until morning light. She tells him in the morning, when he's sober. That's the day after a feast fit for a king.
The answer is that his heart fails within him. When Nabal hears, “…his heart failed within him, and he became like a stone.” It's a heavy moment, so I'll say it plainly. I think this one hurts.
The answer is that the LORD strikes him dead. About ten days later, the text says, “…the LORD struck Nabal dead.” This is a serious moment, friends, so I'll leave it plain.

The answer is his own wickedness. David says, “For the LORD has brought the wickedness of Nabal down upon his own head.” It's about Nabal's own wickedness. David also says the LORD “…has restrained His servant from evil.”
The answer is wife. David sends word to Abigail, asking her to become his wife. His servants then come to her at Carmel and say, “David has sent us to take you as his wife.”
The answer is False. Abigail hurried, got on a donkey and followed David's messengers. No dawdling, just a woman on the move.
The answer is False. The text says David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel. So Ahinoam and Abigail were both his wives.
The answer is True. Saul had given his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim. That's the closing verse of the chapter. It still calls Michal David's wife.
